p.src: After Consort Jia returned to the palace, she appeared before the Emperor the next day to thank him for his favor and report on her visit home, at which His Majesty was greatly pleased. He also had colored silks, gold, silver, and other articles issued from the imperial treasury and bestowed upon Jia Zheng and the various ladies of the inner palace, but there is no need to dwell on this. Meanwhile, in the Rong and Ning mansions, everyone was utterly weary in body and spirit after days of exhausting effort, and it took another two or three days to put away all the furnishings and utensils from the garden. Of them all, Xifeng had the most affairs to manage and the heaviest responsibilities. Others might steal a little rest or seek some quiet, but she alone could not escape her duties; moreover, being proud by nature and unwilling to invite criticism, she struggled on as though she had nothing the matter with her. Baoyu, by contrast, had the least to do and the most leisure of anyone. As it happened, early that morning Xiren's mother came in person to ask Grandmother Jia's permission to take Xiren home for the New Year tea, and she would not return until evening. Baoyu therefore amused himself with the maids by throwing dice and playing a chasing game with weiqi stones. He was playing listlessly in his room when some maids suddenly came to announce, “Master Zhen from the eastern mansion invites you over to watch the opera and see the lanterns.” On hearing this, Baoyu ordered that his clothes be changed. Just as he was about to leave, some sweet steamed curds bestowed by Consort Jia arrived. Remembering how much Xiren had enjoyed them last time, Baoyu ordered that they be saved for her. He then informed Grandmother Jia and went over to watch the opera.

p.src: As it turned out, the pieces being performed at Jia Zhen's included Ding Lang Acknowledges His Father, Huang Boyang Sets Out the Great Array of Departed Spirits, Sun the Pilgrim Raises Havoc in Heaven, and Jiang Ziya Beheads the Generals and Invests the Gods. Now gods and ghosts swarmed wildly across the stage, now demons and monsters revealed themselves in full; there were even processions with banners, invocations of the Buddha, and offerings of incense, while the clamor of gongs, drums, and shouting carried far beyond the lane. Everyone in the street praised it, saying, “What a splendid, bustling performance! No other household could possibly stage such a thing.” Baoyu found the splendor and commotion quite unbearable. After sitting only a short while, he slipped away to amuse himself elsewhere. First he went into the inner quarters and chatted and joked for a while with Madam You, the maids, and the concubines; then he came back out through the second gate. Madam You and the others assumed that he had gone back out to watch the opera and so paid him no further attention. Jia Zhen, Jia Lian, Xue Pan, and the rest were absorbed in drinking games and every kind of merriment and took no notice either. Even if they missed him from his seat for a time, they merely supposed that he had gone inside and did not inquire. As for Baoyu's pages, the older ones knew that now he had arrived the entertainment would not end until night. Seizing their chance, some slipped away to gamble, some went to relatives or friends for New Year tea, and still others went whoring or drinking; all dispersed privately, intending to return in the evening. The younger boys had all burrowed into the backstage rooms to enjoy the spectacle.

p.src: Seeing no one about, Baoyu thought, “There is a little study here where a scroll painting of a beautiful woman usually hangs, and she is portrayed with extraordinary spirit. With all this bustle today, there will surely be no one there, and the beauty herself must be lonely. I ought to go and pay her a visit to comfort her.” With this thought, he made his way to the study. He had just reached the window when he heard sounds of moaning from within. Baoyu started in fright. Could the beauty have come to life? Summoning his courage, he moistened a finger, pierced the paper covering the window, and peered inside. The beauty in the scroll had not come to life; rather, Mingyan had pinned down a young maid and was engaged in the very act taught by Disenchantment. Baoyu could not help crying out, “This is outrageous!” He kicked the door open, startling the pair apart; they trembled as they hurriedly adjusted their clothes.

p.src: When Mingyan saw that it was Baoyu, he hastily fell to his knees and begged for mercy without cease. Baoyu said, “In broad daylight! What do you think you are doing? If Master Zhen finds out, do you imagine you will get out of this alive?” Meanwhile he looked at the girl. Though she was no beauty, she was fair and clean and had something faintly attractive about her. Her face and ears crimson with shame, she stood with bowed head and said nothing. Stamping his foot, Baoyu cried, “Why don't you run, quickly!” His words brought the girl to her senses, and she flew away. Baoyu ran after her and called, “Don't be afraid! I won't tell anyone.” Behind him, Mingyan cried anxiously, “My dear young master, that is as good as telling everyone outright!” Baoyu then asked, “How old is that girl?” Mingyan replied, “No more than sixteen or seventeen.” Baoyu said, “You did not even ask what year she was born in, so naturally you know even less about anything else. Plainly, her acquaintance with you has been entirely wasted. Poor thing, poor thing!” He then asked, “What is her name?” Mingyan laughed heartily. “The story of her name is a long one. It is truly such a strange and novel tale that one could never invent it. According to her, when her mother was carrying her, she dreamed that she received a length of brocade patterned in five colors with an unbroken wan design symbolizing endless wealth and honor. That is why she was named Wan'er.” Baoyu laughed when he heard this. “That truly is unusual. She must surely have some good fortune awaiting her in the future.” Having said this, he fell into thought for a while.

p.src: Xiren’s mother had also come out to welcome him. Xiren took Baoyu by the hand and led him inside. Baoyu saw three or five young girls in the room. When they saw him enter, they all lowered their heads bashfully. Hua Zifang and his mother were desperately afraid that Baoyu might be cold. They invited him onto the kang, hurried to set out a separate table of fruit, and busied themselves pouring him fine tea. Xiren smiled. “You need not put yourselves to needless trouble. I know what he requires. There is no need to set out fruit either, and we must not give him things to eat indiscriminately.” As she spoke, she took her own sitting cushion and spread it on one of the kangs for Baoyu to sit upon. She placed her own foot-warmer beneath his feet, took two plum-blossom incense cakes from her purse, opened her hand-warmer and lit them inside it, then closed it again and put it into Baoyu’s arms. Finally, she poured tea into her own cup and offered it to him. By then, her mother and brother had already hurriedly arranged a neat table laden with fruit. Seeing that there was really nothing among it that he could eat, Xiren smiled and said, “Now that you have come, you cannot leave without taking anything. You must at least taste a little, to mark your visit to my home.” As she spoke, she picked out several pine kernels, blew away their fine skins, placed them on her handkerchief, and offered them to Baoyu.

p.src: Nanny Li then asked, “Is that clotted cream in the covered bowl? Why wasn’t it sent to me? I may as well eat it.” With that, she took up a spoon and began to eat. One maid cried, “Don’t touch it! It was specially set aside for Xiren. When she comes back, there’ll be another quarrel. You’ll have to own up to it yourself, Nanny. Don’t drag us into trouble too.” Hearing this, Nanny Li felt both angry and humiliated. “I refuse to believe he has become so ungrateful. Never mind my eating one bowl of milk—even if it were something more valuable than this, I would still be entitled to it. Can Xiren possibly mean more to him than I do? Doesn’t he remember how he was raised? My blood turned into the milk that nourished him to this size, and now he would be angry because I eat one bowl of his milk? I’m going to eat it, whatever anyone says. Let’s see what happens! You may think Xiren is somebody special, but she’s only a scruffy little girl I trained with my own hands. Who does she think she is?” As she spoke, she defiantly ate every last bit of the clotted cream. Another maid said with a smile, “They don’t know how to speak properly, so no wonder you’re angry, Nanny. Baoyu often sends you gifts to show his respect. How could he possibly take offense over this?” Nanny Li said, “There’s no need for you to put on those foxy airs and wheedle me. Do you imagine I don’t know that Qianxue was driven out last time over a cup of tea? The next time anything goes wrong, I’ll come back and take the blame!” With that, she left in a huff.

Can Xiren possibly mean more to him than I do?
Doesn’t he remember how he was raised?
My blood turned into the milk that nourished him to this size, and now he would be angry because I eat one bowl of his milk?
I’m going to eat it, whatever anyone says. Let’s see what happens!
You may think Xiren is somebody special, but she’s only a scruffy little girl I trained with my own hands. Who does she think she is?”

With that, she left in a huff.

Then he said, “But surely the Old Lady will refuse to let you go.” “Why should she refuse?” asked Xiren. “If I truly were quite irreplaceable, I might perhaps have won the Old Lady’s heart so completely that she would refuse to release me. I came here as a child and attended the Old Lady. First I served Miss Shi for several years, and now I have served you for several more. Now that my family has come to redeem me, it is only proper that I should be allowed to go. The Old Lady may even waive the redemption money and graciously release me. There is absolutely no chance that they would refuse to release me merely because I have served you well. Serving you well is only my proper duty, not some extraordinary achievement. After I leave, another good maid will come in my place. Things will not cease to function merely because I am gone.” Everything she said supplied reasons for her going and none for her staying, and Baoyu grew increasingly anxious. “Even so,” he said, “if I am set on keeping you, the Old Lady will surely speak to your mother. I am not some ordinary object which, because you happen to like it, can be procured for you at ten times the price without the seller suffering any loss. To keep me here without cause would do you no real good and would instead separate flesh and blood. Neither the Old Lady nor Her Ladyship would ever consent to such a thing.” Baoyu listened and pondered for a long while. p.src: Now Xiren had known since childhood that Baoyu possessed an extraordinary nature. His mischievous, foolishly playful ways surpassed those of all other boys, and he had several other exceedingly strange faults that words could scarcely describe. Lately, relying on his grandmother's indulgence—and since even his parents could not keep him under very strict control—he had grown still more unrestrained and undisciplined, following every whim and passion and caring least of all for serious pursuits. Whenever she wished to admonish him, she knew he would not listen. Today, however, the discussion of redeeming her had presented a timely opportunity, so she had first used a false pretext to test his feelings and humble his spirit, after which she could more readily offer him earnest counsel. Now that she saw him lying there in silence, she knew that his tender feelings made it unbearable and that his defiance had subsided. She had never really wanted the chestnuts; she had asked for them only because she feared the cream might cause another quarrel like the earlier affair over Qianxue's tea. By using the chestnuts as a pretext, she could simply gloss over the matter without mentioning it to Baoyu again. She therefore told the little maids to take the chestnuts away and eat them, then went over to rouse Baoyu. She found his face covered with tear stains. Xiren smiled and said, “What is there to grieve about? I hardly know what else to say.” Xiren smiled. “There is no need to speak of how well we have always got along. But if you sincerely wish me to remain today, that is not what matters. p.src: At that moment, Daiyu was taking her afternoon rest in bed. The maids had all gone out to amuse themselves, and the whole room was perfectly still. Baoyu lifted the soft embroidered curtain and entered the inner chamber. Seeing Daiyu asleep there, he hurried over, nudged her, and said, “Dear little sister, you’ve only just eaten, and now you’re sleeping again.” With that, he woke Daiyu. When Daiyu saw that it was Baoyu, she said, “Go out and stroll about for a while. p.src: Taken aback by the question, Baoyu could not make sense of it at first. “What ‘warm fragrance’?” he asked. Daiyu nodded, sighing and laughing. “Fool, fool! You have jade, so someone else has gold to match you. If she has ‘cold fragrance,’ shouldn’t you have ‘warm fragrance’ to match it?” Only then did Baoyu understand her meaning. Baoyu laughed. “You begged for mercy only a moment ago, and now you’re saying even worse things.” As he spoke, he reached out again. Daiyu hurriedly laughed and said, “Dear brother, I truly won’t dare again.” Baoyu said with a smile, “I’ll spare you, but only if you let me smell your sleeve.” With that, he pulled her sleeve over his face and kept breathing in its fragrance. Daiyu snatched it away and said, “Surely it’s time you left now.” Baoyu laughed. “Leave? I can’t. Let’s lie here quietly and have a proper talk.” With that, he lay down again. Daiyu lay down as well. She covered her face with her handkerchief. Baoyu rambled on with one piece of nonsense after another, but Daiyu ignored him. Baoyu asked how old she had been when she came to the capital, what scenery and ancient sites she had seen on the journey, and what historic remains, old stories, local customs, and folkways there were in Yangzhou. Daiyu would not answer.

p.src: Baoyu, afraid that sleeping so much might make her ill, tried to amuse her. “Oh! There is a remarkable tale about your yamen in Yangzhou. Have you heard it?” Seeing how solemnly he spoke, with such a grave and stern expression, Daiyu took it for a true story and asked, “What tale?” At her question, Baoyu suppressed a laugh and improvised, “In Yangzhou there is a Mount Dai. On that mountain is a Wood-rat Cave.” Daiyu laughed. “If you must lie, at least do it properly. I have never heard of such a mountain.” “There are countless mountains and rivers under heaven,” said Baoyu. “How could you possibly know them all? Wait until I have finished before you criticize.” “Go on, then,” said Daiyu. Baoyu resumed his fabrication. “A band of mouse spirits once lived in Wood-rat Cave. On the seventh day of the twelfth month one year, the old mouse took his seat to hold council and said, ‘Tomorrow is the Laba Festival, when everyone in the human world cooks Laba porridge. Our cave is running short of fruit, so this is the perfect chance to raid them for some.’ He drew out a command arrow and dispatched a capable young mouse to investigate. Before long the young mouse returned and reported, ‘I have searched and made inquiries everywhere. The temple at the foot of the mountain alone has the greatest stores of grain and fruit.’ The old mouse asked, ‘How many kinds of grain are there? And how many varieties of fruit?’ The young mouse replied, ‘Their granaries are full of grain and beans, too many to count. There are five kinds of fruit and produce: first, red dates; second, chestnuts; third, peanuts; fourth, water chestnuts; and fifth, fragrant taros.’ The old mouse was delighted and immediately began assigning mice to the raid. Drawing out a command arrow, he asked, ‘Who will steal the grain?’ One mouse accepted the order and went to steal the grain. He drew another command arrow and asked, ‘Who will steal the beans?’ Another mouse accepted the order and went to steal the beans. In this way, each mouse received an assignment and departed. Only the fragrant taros remained, so he drew another command arrow and asked, ‘Who will steal the fragrant taros?’ A very small and feeble young mouse answered, ‘I am willing to steal the fragrant taros.’ Seeing what he was like, the old mouse and the others feared that he lacked experience and was too timid and weak, so none would permit him to go. The young mouse said, ‘Though I am young and frail, my magical powers are boundless, my tongue is clever, and my schemes are far-sighted. I assure you, my theft will be cleverer than any of theirs.’ The mice eagerly asked, ‘How will yours be cleverer than theirs?’ The young mouse said, ‘I shall not imitate them by stealing outright. I shall transform myself into a fragrant taro and roll into the taro pile, where no one will see or hear me. Then, secretly using the art of multiplying my body, I shall carry them away little by little until none remain. Would that not be cleverer than simply stealing them by force?’ When the mice heard this, they all said, ‘It is ingenious indeed, but we do not know how you perform this transformation. Change first and let us see.’ The young mouse laughed. ‘That is easy. Watch me transform.’
